newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bankruptcies at record levels this year.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bankruptcies at record levels this year.

text.p: Bankruptcies of Argentine businesses have hit record levels this year despite other indicators showing a rebound in the economy, the risk rating firm Central de Riesgo Crediticio Fidelitas said Wednesday.
In the first 11 months of 1996, bankruptcies rose 35 percent from the same period a year earlier to a record 1,069.
In the month of November, meanwhile, bankruptcies dropped 14 percent from October to 144.

"Even though other good indicators of the economy are showing a gradual rebound in activity, the accumulated credit risk figures for November show 1996 to be a record year in terms of bankruptcies and closures of current accounts," Raul Ramirez March, manager of Fidelitas, said in a statement.

Closures of corporate current accounts rose to 8,312 in the first 11 months of the year, seven percent higher than in the same period last year. The figure for the first 11 months also represented an all time high for the period.

"The amount of bankruptcies, the amount of voluntary bankruptcies and the number of firms in the capital seeking protection from creditors in the courts do not in themselves yet show a consolidation of the rebound in the economy," said Ramirez March.
The government has reported third quarter economic growth of 6.6 percent and a strong rebound in industrial production, while unemployment remains stubbornly high at 17.1 percent.
